summary: tools/ownership.mjs was over-reporting live claims for two structural reasons, not agent forgetfulness alone: (1) 78 of 452 status files record completion in a field named "status", not "state", which the tool never read, so all 78 displayed as state "?" and counted live regardless of what they said (20 literally say status:"done", 31 say "complete"); (2) the terminal-word regex had no word boundaries on compound machine-generated strings like "builder_delivery_complete". Fixed both, added a narrow tested pattern for "awaiting...critic" (the dispatch's own built_awaiting_critic calibration case), excluded .gitattributes merge=union paths (reports/blog-feed.jsonl) from conflict computation (45.6% of the original 7422 conflicts were pure noise about that one shared append-only file), and added git-log-based freshness (age + [STALE?] hint) to every report -- mtime was tried first and found to be bulk-stamped identically across hundreds of files by checkout/bank passes, not a real edit-recency signal. Self-test: 9 arms, all passing, both directions of every fix. Result: 208 -> 60 live claims from the structural fix alone, -> 56 after 4 individually-verified manual clears. Conflicts: 7422 -> 330 -> 270. All 3 named calibration cases (province.js, dialogue/topics, exterior.js) matched the dispatch's known answers; the one numeric difference (exterior.js now shows 1 live, not 0) is new legitimate work dispatched today, documented as such, not a classifier disagreement.
